record.paper_title: Some open problems in low dimensional dynamical systems
record.original_question: Let T(n) denote the maximum number of critical periods of planar polynomial differential systems of degree n. Determine whether there exists a constant C > 0 such that T(n) ≥ C n² log n.

evidence.quote: Problem 14. Is it true that T (n)≥Cn2 log(n) for some C >0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider planar polynomial differential systems of the form
  x' = P(x,y),  y' = Q(x,y),
where P, Q ∈ ℝ[x,y] have degree at most n, and which possess a center (a singular point all of whose nearby orbits are closed). On the period annulus of such a center, the period function p(s) assigns to each closed orbit (parameterized by some transverse parameter s) its minimal period. A critical period is an isolated critical point of p. Define T(n) to be the supremum, over all planar polynomial systems of degree at most n with a center, of the number of critical periods of the period function on the period annulus.

Determine whether there exists a constant C > 0 such that
  T(n) ≥ C · n² · log n
for all sufficiently large n.
artifact.category_tag: critical periods of planar polynomial centers
artifact.status_search_result: The lower bound T(n) ≥ C n² log n for the maximum number of critical periods of planar polynomial centers of degree n appears to remain an open problem. Recent work (e.g., on critical periods near a maximum number of cusps) has produced improved lower bounds on the number of critical periods for polynomial centers, but the search did not find a confirmation of an n² log n lower bound, and optimality is not established.

status_evidence.title: Critical periods in planar polynomial centers near a maximum number of cusps
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work provides the best known lower bound for the number of critical periods of planar polynomial centers, but no claim of optimality.
status_evidence.claim: Best known lower bounds have been improved but the n² log n bound is not established.

status_evidence.claim: The question is listed as an open problem.
